chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: How the Goodman exposure helped Webb and Sampson
summary: Goodman recorded "Blue Lou" and "Don't Be That Way", boosting Webb's book and leading to the battle.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands

blocks.x: air time. He got more air time that we got, you know. He's on a coast to coast show, you know. Not only that, he began to make Chick's music popular, because all these things come out of Chick's book. That really helped him. Really helped the writer, really helped Sampson, and helped the band. Because they were playing the thing. Every time he would play something and we would play it, "Oh that's Chick Webb's thing," you know. "That's Edgar Sampson, too." That helped us right up on top, you know. And then one thing led into -- the record -- to the battle of the music between Chick Webb and Benny Goodman. That led to the battle of the music, which was also good. One hand helped the other. Benny helped us and in one way we helped him. And it just worked out good for both parties, you know. And that worked into -- And the only thing (Inaudible) just with one song, you know.

Just one song. 'Stompin At The Savoy.' Benny Goodman went on to record 'Blue Lou,' 'Don't Be That Way' -- everything Sampson ever had written he recorded it -- for Sampson. And also, all those things were big numbers in Chick Webb's book.
